title: Jones Beach Drift Whale Rights
summary: Records connect Tackapousha and Native communities with asserted rights to valuable marine resources, including drift whales along the south shore barrier beaches. The modern Jones Beach landscape is therefore also a place to discuss Native jurisdiction, marine economies, and colonial legal change.
address_label: Jones Beach barrier beach landscape, Jones Inlet vicinity
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as part of the south shore/barrier beach history; also connected with Massapequa leadership and overlapping regional authority.
why_this_matters: Jones Beach is usually remembered as a modern public beach, but older records connect the barrier island to Native marine rights and coastal economies. The site carries histories of Indigenous jurisdiction and resource knowledge within a familiar public landscape.
introduction_content: The location is shown broadly because this history concerns a long barrier beach and a resource-rights landscape rather than a single pinpoint site.
